image_prompt.text: Repeating park clutter - trees, benches, hedges, play equipment - arranged in clusters so a runner can break the tagger's line and cut around
A warren-like corner of the park with hedged corridors to be hunted through
A gathering spot at the park entrance where players wait between rounds
an open park to run around in - grass, winding paths, open ground between the clutter

layout_placement.text: Tag detection between the player who is it and everyone else, passing it on contact
a round timer volume that eliminates whoever is it when time runs out

notes: obstacle-maze comes from the preset and carries P6, which is the only pipeline cost on this build. Dropping it returns the route to P0.
Win condition is last man standing by elimination, which no field in the handoff carries.

open_questions.ask: No look was given - should the park read as bright and stylised, or an ordinary modern city park?

coverage_missing.ask: Bright and cartoony, or a realistic city park?
Do eliminated players spectate, or leave the round entirely?
How many players per round, and how big does the park need to be for them?

answers.ask: No look was given - should the park read as bright and stylised, or an ordinary modern city park?
answers.answer: Make it a bright, stylised park so the tag game is easy to read and playful.

answers.ask: How big should the park be - one open field you can cross in a few seconds, or a whole park with several areas?
answers.answer: Use one small open park field that players can cross in a few seconds; keep the first build simple and focused.

answers.ask: Where do eliminated players go while the round finishes?
answers.answer: Eliminated players should go to a simple spectator area above or beside the park and watch until the round ends.
